title: Image Analysis to Quantify Coral Bleaching Using Greyscale Model
author: Rowan McLachlan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bx8wprxe

steps.title: Download ImageJ software
steps.instruction: Download the free ImageJ program from the NIH website (https://imagej.nih.gov/ij/download.html).

steps.title: Import coral photograph
steps.instruction: Open ImageJ and import the first photograph of the coral fragment (either the top view or side view) into the program.

steps.title: Convert image to 8‑bit greyscale
steps.instruction: In ImageJ select Image → Type → 8‑bit to convert the colour photograph to an 8‑bit greyscale (black‑and‑white) image.

steps.title: Zoom, position, and draw first circle
steps.instruction: Use the hand tool and zoom (Ctrl + + on PC keyboard or mouse scroll) until the coral fills the ImageJ window; then select the Oval tool (second button from left) and draw a circular region on the coral, avoiding shadows or glare.

substeps.instruction: Zoom in using Ctrl + + (or mouse scroll) until the coral fills the window
Select the Oval tool and draw a circle on a clear area of the coral, avoiding shadows or glare

steps.title: Configure measurements
steps.instruction: Open Analyze → Set Measurements, check the box for “Mean grey value”, and confirm.

steps.title: Measure first region
steps.instruction: With the circle selected, choose Analyze → Measure (or press Ctrl + M) to record the X, Y coordinates and mean grey value for that region; the result appears in the Results window.

steps.title: Measure five coral circles
steps.instruction: Repeat drawing a new circle on a different, shadow‑free area of the coral and measuring it (Analyze → Measure) until you have measured five distinct coral regions.

substeps.instruction: Draw a new circle on a different coral area avoiding shadows/glare

steps.title: Measure white reference area
steps.instruction: Draw a circle of similar size on the white background (paper standard), avoiding shadows, glare, or dirt, and measure its mean grey value.

steps.title: Measure second set of circles
steps.instruction: Draw and measure five new coral circles (distinct from previous ones) and one additional white reference circle, following the same size and avoidance criteria.

steps.title: Copy values to Excel
steps.instruction: Copy the twelve mean grey values (five coral + five coral + two references) from the Results window and paste them into an Excel spreadsheet, formatting as shown in Fig. 10.

steps.title: Repeat with side view image
steps.instruction: Perform steps 2–10 using the side‑view photograph, then paste those values next to the top‑view values in the same spreadsheet (resulting in n = 10 coral values per view and four reference values).

steps.title: Normalize to white reference
steps.instruction: Normalize each coral mean grey value to its corresponding white reference mean using the equation provided in Fig. 12 (e.g., circles #1‑#5 to White Std1, #6‑#10 to White Std2, #11‑#15 to White Std3, #16‑#20 to White Std4).

steps.title: Calculate MIG and SD
steps.instruction: In the spreadsheet compute the mean intensity grey (MIG) and standard deviation of the 20 normalized values using the formula shown in Fig. 13.
